strategies.comments:
Offensive EV Benchmarks

  • 44 SpA: This lets Thunderclap OHKO offensive Urshifu-R.

  • 140 SpA: This 2HKOes Modest Ursaluna-B that have maximum HP and Special Defense investment with Tera Blast + Draco Meteor if using Booster Energy.

  • 204 SpA: This lets +2 Thunderbolt OHKO offensive Flutter Mane.

Defensive EV Benchmarks

  • 140 HP This is the minimum amount of HP needed to survive Annihilape's Final Gambit.

  • 148 HP / 20 Def: This lets Raging Bolt survive +1 Jolly Ogerpon-H's Play Rough.

  • 140 HP / 76 SpD: This avoid a 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane after Sitrus Berry Raging Bolt has a Calm Mind boost.

  • 140 HP / 108 Def: This survives Adamant Choice Band Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch.

  • 140 HP / 180 Def: This survives Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquale and Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash.

  • 20 HP / 172 Def: This is the most EV efficient way to survive Adamant Choice Band Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch, at the cost of being OHKOed by Annihilape's Final Gambit.

Assault Vest EV Benchmarks

  • 140 HP / 92 SpD: This survives Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • 140 HP / 132 SpD: This avoids a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Stealth Rock damage if Raging Bolt is Terastallized.

Speed EV Benchmarks

  • 44 Spe: This outspeeds minimum Speed Dragonite.

  • 76 Spe: This outspeeds maximum Speed Modest Ursaluna-B.

  • 132 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Ursaluna, a rare but powerful threat against Raging Bolt.

  • 156 Spe: This outspeeds Timid Ursaluna-B.

  • 220 Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Breloom, a rare threat that can stop Raging Bolt's sweeps with Spore.

  • 196+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Basculegion.

  • 204+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Dragonite.

  • 244+ Spe: This outspeeds Modest Archaludon.

movesets.name: Bulky Offense
movesets.description:
• Raging Bolt's decent defensive typing, hefty bulk, and booming priority in Thunderclap make it an excellent bulky offensive Pokemon.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge versus Volt Switch: Volt Switch makes Raging Bolt a great pivot, but it does mean that Raging Bolt lacks a reliable Electric-type STAB move or has worse coverage, making Thunderbolt a reasonable alternative. Discharge's higher paralysis chance can make the power drop worth it if using slow teammates like Ursaluna-B.

  • Heavy Slam: When used with a Quiet nature, Heavy Slam OHKOes offensive Flutter Mane! If using Modest, it'll still put most Flutter Mane into Thunderclap's KO range as well.

  • Modest versus Quiet: Quiet is mainly used for OHKOing offensive Flutter Mane with Heavy Slam, but even with that move, Modest makes sense if your team requires Speed investment.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Raging Bolt's good typing means Terastallization does have some drawbacks, such as making Urshifu-R harder to switch-into, but it has enough common weaknesses to types like Ground and Fairy that mean Terastallization will often be optimal.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a fantastic defensive typing, making Raging Bolt a spectacular check to most Urshifu-S and prancing around strong Dragon-type attacks.

  • Steel: Retaining the common Ground weakness is unfortunate, but Tera Steel makes up for it by tanking Fairy-type attacks and shredding Flutter Mane with Heavy Slam.

  • Ice: When used with Tera Blast, Tera Ice chills Landorus-T to the bone and deals tremendous damage to Ursaluna-B without firing off Draco Meteor.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Raging Bolt a cool resistance to Ice-type attacks from the likes of Chien-Pao while still retaining the Surging Strikes resistance against Urshifu-R. Just watch out for Tera Electric Chien-Pao.

  • Electric: Tera Electric makes sense for making Thunderclap an even more effective revenge killing tool and ridding Raging Bolt of its Fairy and Dragon weaknesses.

  • Bug: This niche Tera type grants Raging Bolt a resistance to Ground without making it weak to Ice.

EV Spread Examples

  • 148 HP / 156 Def / 204 SpA with Modest or Quiet: This survives both Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake and Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash on all but the highest roll of damage, and it also OHKOes offensive Flutter Mane with +2 Thunderbolt.

  • 148 HP / 20 Def / 180 SpA / 4 SpD / 156 Spe with Modest: This spread outspeeds the rare but dangerous Timid Ursaluna-B while avoiding an OHKO from Timid Flutter Mane's unboosted Moonblast and +1 Ogerpon-H's Play Rough.

  • 140 HP / 236 SpA / 132 SpD with Modest or Quiet: These EVs are optimized for Assault Vest, letting Terastallized Raging Bolt to avoid a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Stealth Rock damage.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet lets Raging Bolt punish Urshifu-R that lack Punching Glove for using Surging Strikes, since most Urshiu-R will switch out from Raging Bolt.

  • Booster Energy: Booster Energy gives Raging Bolt a useful increase in power, with Thunderbolt now OHKOing Primarina that lack Assault Vest. However, it doesn't work well with Volt Switch and will usually tell your opponent that you aren't carrying it.

  • Weakness Policy: Raging Bolt is bulky enough to take full advantage of Weakness Policy, turning Thunderclap into a vicious cleaning tool!

  • Assault Vest: Raging Bolt's excellent bulk and pivoting prowess make it a great user of Assault Vest.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's quick burst of recovery is especially helpful when Terastallized into a type that doesn't resist Water against Urshifu-R. Just make sure to use an even HP number to eat the Berry after being hit by Ruination once.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs transforms Raging Bolt into a fearsome wallbreaking pivot! However, it makes Thunderclap even riskier to use.

movesets.name: Calm Mind
movesets.description:
• Raging Bolt's incredible bulk and access to the crackling Thunderclap make it one of the most dangerous special attackers in the metagame!

  • Dragon Pulse versus Draco Meteor: Dragon Pulse is a reliable STAB attack against Ground-type foes. Draco Meteor is harder to sweep teams with, but it severely damages Assault Vest Ursaluna-B enough that it's worth considering.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: A reliable Electric-type attack ensures that the risky Thunderclap isn't Raging Bolt's only option against Water-types, with Thunderbolt offering a tad more power, while Discharge's 30% paralysis rate is helpful for slow teammates like Ursaluna-B and Basculegion.

  • Volt Switch with Draco Meteor: Volt Switch may seem completely contrary to sweeping with Calm Mind boosts, but it can be combined with Draco Meteor to transform Raging Bolt into a wallbreaking pivot rather than a bulky sweeper.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Raging Bolt's common weaknesses like Ground and Fairy, combined with its awesome bulk, makes it a good candidate for Terastallization to prevent revenge kills.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a brilliant defensive typing, ruining Dragon-type attacks and transforming Raging Bolt into a good Urshifu-S check in a pinch.

  • Water: Tera Water is perfect for soaking up Ice-type attacks from Chien-Pao while still resisting Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes.

  • Electric: In addition to removing the annoying Fairy and Dragon weaknesses, Tera Electric makes Thunderclap an even more fearsome priority attack!

  • Ice: Tera Ice is awful defensively, but when paired with Tera Blast, Raging Bolt can freeze specially defensive Landorus-T's smug grin off with an OHKO!

  • Steel Steel unfortunately retains that annoying Ground weakness, but the resistance to Dragon and Fairy is good enough to consider it against threats like Flutter Mane and offensive Archaludon.

  • Bug: This niche Tera type gives Raging Bolt a Ground resistance without an Ice weakness that would doom it against Chien-Pao like Tera Flying would.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers rewards Raging Bolt's longevity more than any item, making it the prime cut of items.

  • Rocky Helmet: With Rocky Helmet, Raging Bolt can consistently punish Choice Scarf Urshifu-R for using Surging Strikes, giving it the perfect chance to set up Calm Mind as Urshifu-R switches out.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can be used with specalized EV spreads to prevent some useful 2HKOs. Just make sure to use an even HP stat so it's eaten after Raging Bolt is hit by Ruination one time.

  • Booster Energy: Booster Energy is a more immediately offensive approach to Raging Bolt, letting it deal good damage without needing to set up Calm Mind.

  • Figy, Aguav, Mago, Iapapa, or Wiki Berry: These berries restore more health than Sitrus Berry, though the 25% HP activation does make them riskier.

EV Spread Examples

  • 140 HP / 180 Def / 44 SpA / 140 SpD / 4 Spe: This spread survives Annihilape's Final Gambit, Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake, and Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash. It also OHKOes offensive Urshifu-R with Thunderclap and survives Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Stealth Rock damage.

  • 148 HP / 20 Def / 180 SpA / 4 SpD / 156 Spe with Modest: This Raging Bolt is fast enough to outspeed Timid Ursaluna-B, a rare but potentially game-ending threat! The defensive investment ensures that Raging Bolt survives a +1 Play Rough from Jolly Ogerpon-H and Moonblast from Timid Flutter Mane.

  • 140 HP / 4 Def / 244 SpA / 76 SpD / 44 Spe: This lets Sitrus Berry Raging Bolt avoid a 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Raging Bolt boosts with Calm Mind, and it also outspeeds minimum Speed Dragonite.

strategies.overview:
• Raging Bolt, with a higher Special Attack than Flutter Mane, massive HP, and good defenses, serves its role as a bulky damage dealer exceptionally well.

  • Don't let Raging Bolt's middling Speed fool you; its signature move, Thunderclap, prevents it from being an issue in a lot of situations and makes the Tornadus + Urshifu-R matchup virtually trivial. Raging Bolt is also really strong into the Ogerpon formes and Rillaboom, as it resists all of their STAB moves except Ogerpon-C's, unless the Ogerpon-H and Rillaboom are carrying Stomping Tantrum and High Horsepower as coverage, respectively.

  • Raging Bolt pairs insanely well with Rillaboom and Incineroar, as they provide Fake Out pressure for Raging Bolt to take advantage of by lowering the foe's Special Attack or Speed on the Assault Vest set, set up with the Calm Mind set or deal massive damage with the three attacks set. Rillaboom also provides more longevity in Grassy Terrain for Raging Bolt, which can make it immensely difficult to KO. Chien-Pao and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R are also excellent partners thanks to dealing with Raging Bolt's worst matchup, Landorus.

  • That said, Raging Bolt does still have bad matchups, one of which is the aforementioned Landorus due to it being able to threaten an OHKO against Raging Bolt with Earth Power. Chien-Pao can also be a tricky matchup, as it can deal massive damage with its Ice-type STAB move and cause mindgames with Sucker Punch. Flutter Mane is able to deal huge damage to Raging Bolt even when it Terastallizes and can very comfortably take unboosted Thunderclaps.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
• Electroweb is sometimes run over Thunderbolt for speed control. Volt Switch allows for Raging Bolt to become a bulky pivot and pairs well with Draco Meteor, allowing it to switch out after the Special Attack drop. Snarl weakens opposing special attackers, enabling it to sit on the field for longer and deal damage. Tera Blast gives Raging Bolt a strong option into bulky Dark-types and Fighting-types like Ting-Lu and Iron Hands.

  • Assault Vest allows Raging Bolt to fully take advantage of its amazing bulk, letting it sit on the field and tank hit after hit all while dealing respectable damage and disrupting the foe with moves like Snarl and Electroweb.

  • The defensive investment allows Raging Bolt to always survive Icicle Crash from Adamant Chien-Pao and Moonblast from Choice Specs Flutter Mane. The Speed investment allows Raging Bolt to outspeed Glimmora and Modest Chi-Yu after an Electroweb. The rest of the EVs were put into offensive investment.

  • Tera Fairy is just an incredibly strong neutral Tera type, especially for a Pokemon with as much bulk as Raging Bolt has, and provides a resistance to Urshifu-S's STAB moves.

movesets.name: Calm Mind
movesets.description:
• Thunderclap is a good main STAB move, as it allows Raging Bolt to focus less on Speed and go all out on bulk investment, as it will be able to boost up then hit most foes before they can retaliate.

  • While Dragon Pulse is usually an underwhelming move, it serves as a strong neutral STAB move into Pokemon that resist Electric-type attacks when paired with Calm Mind.

  • In some situations, Thunderbolt can be used over Protect, due to Raging Bolt being bulky enough to where Protect isn't mandatory on Calm Mind sets, and for consistency against support Pokémon such as Follow Me Ogerpon-W where Thunderclap would fail.

  • Leftovers is preferred on the Calm Mind set, providing immense longevity with Grassy Terrain from Rillaboom.

  • The Defense EVs with the HP EVs allow Raging Bolt to live Icicle Crash from Adamant Chien-Pao. The HP EVs make the HP optimized for Leftovers and Grassy Terrain recovery. The bulk investment ensures that Raging Bolt is able to tank 2 unboosted Moonblasts from Timid Flutter Mane at +1 Special Defense after Leftovers and Grassy Terrain recovery combined with Protect. The Special Defense EVs hit an even number to be optimal for the Calm Mind boost.

  • Raging Bolt utilizes Tera Fairy for the resistance to Urshifu-S's STAB moves and neutral matchup against the majority of the metagame.

movesets.name: 3 Attacks
movesets.description:
• Thunderbolt provides good consistent damage, especially with Tera Electric, while Thunderclap helps make up for Raging Bolt's middling Speed. Draco Meteor is a more powerful option, being able to OHKO Pokémon like Landorus when used with Booster Energy. However, it can be forced to switch out after a Special Attack drop and lose the boost.

  • Booster Energy is a strong option, as boosting Raging Bolt's already huge base Special Attack even further turns it into an absolute nuke. Safety Goggles prevents Amoonguss from redirecting Thunderclaps away from Urshifu-R.

  • The Speed investment allows Raging Bolt to outspeed Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao while under Tailwind, allowing it to hit them with its stronger options like Thunderbolt and Draco Meteor.

  • Tera Grass is a good option to not only resist Ground-type moves from Landorus but also ignore Amoonguss's Spore and redirection with Rage Powder without running Safety Goggles. Tera Electric will often be a consistent option for just raw damage output.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
Raging Bolt is an incredibly bulky special attacker that can stay on the field and survive hits from Restricted Pokemon, and threaten them back with its huge Special Attack stat and weaken their team with stat reducing moves. It matches up incredibly well into Urshifu-R, keeping it in check with Thunderclap, Koraidon, since it commonly doesn't run Dragon-type moves, common Fire / Water / Grass cores, which usually have Incineroar, Rillaboom, and Urshifu-R or Ogerpon-W, and multiple strong special attackers with Snarl, such as Kyogre, Calyrex-S, and Terapagos. Electroweb gives Raging Bolt a solid speed control option while still dealing relevant damage. Thunderbolt is a consistent and strong STAB option, and Volt Switch gives it a strong way to reposition itself. Assault Vest allows it to survive hits more easily from strong special attackers such as Calyrex-S, Terapagos, Kyogre, Flutter Mane, and opposing Raging Bolt while punishing them with a Snarl, Electroweb, or stronger attacking move. The EV spread allows it to avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S, survive an Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao, and outspeed -1 Gholdengo and Adamant Urshifu. Tera Electric significantly increases the damage it does at the cost of remaining vulnerable to strong Ground-type attackers such as Landorus and Groudon, while Tera Fairy allows it to gain an immunity to threatening Dragon-type attacks from the likes of Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt while still having a very strong defensive typing into the current metagame.

Raging Bolt synergizes well with multiple Pokemon and can work on many team structures, but some notable partners are Incineroar, since it can reduce the threat from physical moves that Raging Bolt cannot weaken, Koraidon, since it activates Raging Bolt's ability Protosynthesis by setting up sun, and Urshifu-R, which checks multiple strong threats to Raging Bolt like Calyrex-I, Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Landorus. Another Pokemon that checks Raging Bolt is Amoonguss, since Raging Bolt can't stop a Spore from going off and Raging Bolt's attacks can be redirected by Rage Powder without many issues. It is also vulnerable to Fake Out, since Raging Bolt is unable to use Protect to block it because of its Assault Vest, and variants without Draco Meteor can't threaten Incineroar for high damage, allowing it to use Parting Shot and pivot out relatively safely.

movesets.name: Three Attacks
movesets.description:
Raging Bolt is a strong special attacker that uses its good natural bulk and offensive typing to survive attacks and respond with strong Electric- and Dragon-type moves. Draco Meteor gives Raging Bolt a one-time nuke, while Dragon Pulse is a more consistent option for Life Orb sets. Thunderclap allows Raging Bolt to threaten faster Pokemon like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R before they can move. Booster Energy and Life Orb both allow Raging Bolt to deal more damage at the cost of either losing its boost on switch or taking recoil. Life Orb is used on sun teams, as its boost can stack with the Protosynthesis boost. Tera Electric boosts Thunderbolt and Thunderclap, allowing Raging Bolt to OHKO Pokemon such as bulky Kyogre with Thunderbolt and Urshifu-R with Thunderclap if Urshifu-R Terastallizes into a neutral type, as well as 2HKOing Calyrex-I with Thunderbolt. Tera Fairy makes Raging Bolt immune to Dragon-type attacks like Miraidon's Draco Meteor in addition to being a good neutral type.

Raging Bolt struggles into bulky Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Ting-Lu that resist or are immune to Thunderbolt, survive Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse, and respond with Spore or a super effective attack. Faster offensive Pokemon like Miraidon, Zacian-C, and Landorus are also a problem for Raging Bolt, as they can threaten to OHKO it. Calyrex-I threatens the Grass-, Ground-, and Dragon-types that resist Thunderbolt, as well as setting up Trick Room to help Raging Bolt with faster threats. Raging Bolt can also hit the Water-types that resist Glacial Lance with Thunderbolt or Thunderclap. Pokemon that can set up sun such as Koraidon also pair well with Raging Bolt, as they allow it to get a Protosynthesis boost in addition to Life Orb. Raging Bolt can support them by threatening Water-types that resist Flare Blitz or by removing Pelipper, which is a common check to sun teams.

movesets.name: Calm Mind
movesets.description:
Raging Bolt's good natural bulk allows it to function well as a bulky setup sweeper. It has good matchups against Kyogre and Urshifu-R due to STAB Thunderclap. Dragon Pulse is commonly used to break Pokemon that resist Thunderclap, like opposing Raging Bolt and Miraidon. Dragon Pulse may also aid against Pokemon with redirection like Ogerpon-W or Armor Tail Farigiraf that blocks Thunderclap. Leftovers is the preferred item on Calm Mind Raging Bolt due to the increased longevity, especially when paired with Grassy Terrain support from Rillaboom. Alternatively, Raging Bolt can use Booster Energy for an immediate power boost, threatening an OHKO on Miraidon and a 2HKO on Calyrex-S. 244 HP and 52 Defense EVs allow Raging Bolt to survive Adamant Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner. The HP and Special Defense EVs allow +1 Special Defense Terastallized Raging Bolt to survive two attacks from both Modest Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Landorus's Earth Power. 92 Speed EVs allow Raging Bolt to outspeed 4 Speed Rillaboom. Tera Fairy is the Tera type of choice because it provides Raging Bolt an even matchup into most of the format.

Good partners for Calm Mind Raging Bolt include Rillaboom because it can provide Grassy Terrain and create free turns with Fake Out, allowing Raging Bolt to set up more safely. Similarly, Incineroar is often paired with Raging Bolt, since it can offer damage reduction and Fake Out support. Redirection, such as Ogerpon-W's Follow Me, is greatly appreciated by Raging Bolt. Groudon and Koraidon are also good partners for Raging Bolt, since they can activate its Protosynthesis ability and check Pokemon like Amoonguss and Zacian-C, which are common checks for Raging Bolt. Amoonguss threatens Raging Bolt's Thunderclap via Rage Powder redirection and Spore. Zacian-C, Groudon, Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Calyrex-I, and Landorus can threaten Raging Bolt before and after it Terastallizes.

movesets.name: Bulky Special Attacker
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Raging Bolt has phenomenal natural bulk and Special Attack, allowing it to stay on the field while chipping foes, and with priority in Thunderclap, it can finish off low-HP targets. Its potent STAB moves and survivability give it favorable matchups against Kyogre, Urshifu-R, Tornadus, and Koraidon.
  • Although Draco Meteor can miss and weakens Raging Bolt's damage output afterwards, it's used for a higher burst of damage, notably OHKOing non-Assault Vest Miraidon and Raging Bolt as well as Tera Dragon Zamazenta-C. Dragon Pulse is more consistent, lacking those drawbacks, but doesn't offer the same immediate power.
  • Magnet is the most consistent item since Raging Bolt primarily uses Electric-type STAB moves, which get boosted. Life Orb offers a higher damage increase than Magnet and applies to all moves but reduces survivability. Additionally, both Life Orb and Magnet stack with the power boost from Protosynthesis in sun. Booster Energy provides the same boost as Life Orb without the recoil, but the boost is lost after switching out.
  • The Defense investment allows Raging Bolt to live Close Combat from Life Orb Koraidon, Glacial Lance from most Calyrex-I, and almost always live Ice Spinner from Adamant Chien-Pao. The Speed investment enables Raging Bolt to outspeed maximum Speed Koraidon, Chien-Pao, and Miraidon in Tailwind. The rest is put into Special Attack to maximize its damage output.
  • Tera Electric is used to boost its Electric-type STAB moves, notably allowing it to score valuable chip damage on Pokemon like Zamazenta-C with Thunderbolt, even putting it in range of a Thunderclap. It also allows Raging Bolt to OHKO Kyogre with Thunderbolt and the Life Orb and Booster Energy variants to almost always 2HKO non-Leftovers Calyrex-I with Thunderbolt. Tera Electric can also help it live Dragon-, Ice-, and Fairy-type moves such as Draco Meteor from non-Choice Specs Miraidon, Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao, and Moonblast from Flutter Mane.

Teambuilding

  • Raging Bolt struggles against Chien-Pao, which threatens it with Icicle Crash and Ice Spinner, and it can pick Raging Bolt off with priority Sucker Punch, which outspeeds Thunderclap under normal circumstances.
  • Landorus is problematic because it can outspeed and threaten Raging Bolt with Earth Power. Similarly, Ursaluna moves before Raging Bolt under Trick Room and threatens it with Headlong Rush.
  • Calyrex-I and Miraidon teams are major threats, as Glacial Lance and Draco Meteor force Raging Bolt to Terastallize. Additionally, Choice Specs Miraidon can OHKO with Draco Meteor even if Raging Bolt Terastallizes.
  • Zacian-C threatens to OHKO Raging Bolt with Play Rough, and Iron Treads pressures it with High Horsepower while not taking much damage in return.
  • Grimmsnarl's damage mitigation via Light Screen and Spirit Break make it difficult for Raging Bolt to get Pokemon low on HP and finish them off with Thunderclap. Terapagos can tank Raging Bolt's attacks fairly well, especially after setting up with Calm Mind, and it can later pressure with Earth Power. Similarly, Assault Vest Ting-Lu is hard to break; it takes even less from Raging Bolt's Dragon-type moves and can wear it down with Sand Tomb and Snarl.
  • Amoonguss and Brute Bonnet can be troublesome for Raging Bolt, as it can't OHKO them and risks being put to sleep by Spore. They can also redirect Raging Bolt's Thunderclap with Rage Powder, preventing it from hitting their partners.
  • Koraidon is a great partner for Raging Bolt, boosting its damage output through Protosynthesis in sun. It also helps cover several of Raging Bolt’s problem matchups, threatening Amoonguss and Calyrex-I with Flare Blitz and Ting-Lu and Terapagos with Close Combat or Collision Course. In return, Raging Bolt pressures Kyogre with its Electric-type STAB moves.
  • Raging Bolt fits well on Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C balance teams. Calyrex-S can chip foes into Thunderclap range with Astral Barrage, and Raging Bolt can do the same for Calyrex-S, allowing it to receive Grim Neigh boosts. Zamazenta-C helps against Chien-Pao and Terapagos and can block Glacial Lance from Calyrex-I with Wide Guard. Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot can help Raging Bolt survive some of the aforementioned attacks.
  • Rillaboom and Raging Bolt both take hits well and apply priority pressure with Grassy Glide and Thunderclap, respectively. Chien-Pao also synergizes with Raging Bolt by threatening Amoonguss, Brute Bonnet, Miraidon, and Landorus with Icicle Crash or Ice Spinner while also contributing strong priority pressure, making it difficult for foes to attack freely.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Assault Vest Raging Bolt is a great bulky special attacker with excellent versatility and longevity thanks to the Assault Vest and its great natural bulk. It has good matchups against Restricted Pokemon like Koraidon, Kyogre, Lunala, and Calyrex-S and non-Restricted threats such as Urshifu-R, Tornadus, and Ogerpon-H.
  • Draco Meteor can be inconsistent, but it has the power to consistently OHKO threats like Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt, something Dragon Pulse cannot do. Dragon Pulse, while more reliable, lacks that same level of immediate power. Electroweb gives Raging Bolt a form of speed control that still deals meaningful damage, letting it outspeed Pokemon like Kyogre, Chi-Yu, the Urshifu formes, and Lunala after one Electroweb. Snarl allows Raging Bolt to disrupt special attackers like Calyrex-S, Kyogre, Landorus, Terapagos, and Lunala, as well as dealing good damage to Calyrex-S and breaking Lunala's Shadow Shield.
  • Assault Vest lets Raging Bolt take considerably more special attacks from Pokemon such as Calyrex-S, Lunala, Landorus, and Terapagos, such as being able to survive two of Life Orb Calyrex-S's Astral Barrages and two of Lunala's Moongeist Beams.
  • The EV spread allows Raging Bolt to survive Glacial Lance from 116 Attack Adamant Calyrex-I, Icicle Crash from Jolly Chien-Pao, and Close Combat from Life Orb Koraidon. The Special Defense investment lets Raging Bolt survive Life Orb Landorus's Earth Power, two of Life Orb Calyrex-S's Astral Barrages, and Miraidon's Draco Meteor and Electro Drift after Terastallizing. The Speed investment lets Raging Bolt outspeed Landorus after a speed drop while outspeeding Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R in Tailwind.
  • Tera Electric is a great option to let Raging Bolt consistently 2HKO Flutter Mane, Calyrex-S, and Incineroar with Thunderbolt. Tera Fairy is a good general defensive typing to let it take Zamazenta-C's Body Press and become immune to Dragon-type moves from Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt.

Teambuilding

  • Raging Bolt can struggle against Pokemon such as Focus Sash Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane, as both can survive attacks from Raging Bolt and hit it for big damage with Ice Spinner, Icicle Crash, or Moonblast.
  • Raging Bolt has bad matchups against Ground-type Pokemon like Landorus and Ursaluna, which are immune to Electric-type attacks and threaten Raging Bolt. Pokemon with Fake Out, such as Incineroar and Iron Hands, can also do well against this set, as it cannot use Protect to get around Fake Out, and both can take Raging Bolt's attacks well, allowing them to use Parting Shot or Low Kick in return.
  • Raging Bolt synergizes with sun setters like Koraidon, as sun boosts Raging Bolt's Special Attack through Protosynthesis while Raging Bolt provides support for Koraidon against Kyogre. Raging Bolt also supports Pokemon like Calyrex-S against Tornadus and Urshifu-R with Thunderclap and helps Pokemon such as Calyrex-I and Zamazenta-C in the Koraidon matchup.
  • Non-Restricted Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Chien-Pao pair nicely with Raging Bolt by hitting Ground- and Grass-type Pokemon such as Landorus and Rillaboom that Raging Bolt may be bad against. Incineroar is another great partner for Raging Bolt, being able to switch into threats like Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane and weaken Iron Hands and the aforementioned Chien-Pao with Intimidate. Encore Calyrex-S and Incineroar as well as other Fake Out users like Rillaboom help combat opposing Fake Out with Encore or their own Fake Out.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 1 onwards

Price Range: 13-14 points

Tera Price Range: 18-19 points

Overview: Boasting a monstrously high Special Attack stat with great overall bulk, Raging Bolt is able to hit hard while taking hits just as well. Thunderclap lets it clean up games and force opponents to make difficult decisions, and Draco Meteor can nuke foes that are slower than it. With the ability to Terastallize, it can check and break through just about any foe it needs to while giving it more opportunities to set up with Calm Mind if needed. Very little can threaten Raging Bolt, though it often struggles against faster physical wallbreakers, especially ones that can survive a Thunderclap or disrupt it with Substitute or Encore.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Setup Sweeper: Raging Bolt is able to use Calm Mind to break through most teams' defensive cores, firing off STAB moves for slower threats and Thunderclap for faster ones. Booster Energy can give it additional wallbreaking power, while Leftovers gives it more longevity, especially when combined with Substitute. It often utilizes Terastallization to gain valuable coverage as well as a better defensive typing to set up against specific foes.

Bulky Offense: Raging Bolt can focus on checking specific foes while threatening the team with powerful attacks in return. It can set up with Calm Mind for further wallbreaking power, pivot with Volt Switch to maintain momentum while still dealing large amounts of damage, or even run Choice Specs to nuke whatever switches into it.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Thunderclap, Thunderbolt, Discharge, Volt Switch, Draco Meteor, Dragon Pulse

Setup Moves: Calm Mind

Utility Moves: Taunt, Dragon Tail, Thunder Wave, Substitute, Roar

Coverage: Ancient Power, Body Press, Tera Blast

Niche Moves

Sunny Day: Sunny Day allows Raging Bolt to activate Protosynthesis without having to rely on Booster Energy or a teammate with Drought. This move gives it flexibility with its item slot and allows it to use Solar Beam and Weather Ball while granting a damage buff similar to Calm Mind.

Solar Beam: Raging Bolt can use Solar Beam either under sun or with a Power Herb to break through Ground-types that might wall it otherwise.

Weather Ball: On sun teams or with Sunny Day, Weather Ball gives Raging Bolt additional Fire-type coverage to hit bulky Grass- and Steel-types. It can also work as a surprise Ice-type move with snow from either Snow Warning or Chilly Reception.

Common Items

Booster Energy: Booster Energy allows Raging Bolt to begin wallbreaking immediately rather than having to spend a turn setting up. This works best with early- or late-game wallbreaking due to it being a single-use item.

Leftovers: Leftovers provides valuable healing to Raging Bolt, especially when the opponent has poor entry hazard setters or is unable to reliably answer Calm Mind Raging Bolt. This works especially well with Substitute in order to keep it as healthy as possible.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots allows Raging Bolt to remain at full health upon switching in so that it can set up much easier. This item also works well when it wants to switch in frequently in order to check or revenge kill certain foes.

Niche Items

Choice Specs: Choice Specs's increased power can be valuable for immediate wallbreaking if Raging Bolt wants to switch in multiple times a game.

Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is a solid choice compared to Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots if Raging Bolt expects to take one strong hit and needs to remain relatively healthy.

Assault Vest: Assault Vest allows Raging Bolt to utilize its strong defensive typing to check certain specially offensive foes in matchups where it may not need setup to be effective.

Resistance Berry: A resistance Berry can help Raging Bolt set up easier or allow it to pick off a faster threat that it otherwise couldn't.

Mental Herb: Mental Herb prevents Raging Bolt from being susceptible to Encore when trying to set up against faster foes.

Other Damage-boosting Items: If Raging Bolt needs more than a one-time damage boost, items like Life Orb and Magnet let it hit damage benchmarks while not being Choice-locked by Choice Specs.

Eject Pack: Raging Bolt can use Eject Pack in combination with Draco Meteor to damage opposing switch-ins that could otherwise tank its attacks and pivot out.

Power Herb: Power Herb is ran with Solar Beam to break through specific Ground-types that would otherwise wall Raging Bolt.

Tera

Raging Bolt is one of the best Tera Captains in the format, so it should always be drafted with the intent of being one. It benefits massively from both offensive and defensive Tera types. Offensively, it's able to strengthen its already strong Thunderclap and Draco Meteor with STAB Tera types, and it can choose types such as Tera Water and Grass to gain needed coverage against Ground-types. Defensively, it's able to utilize Tera Fairy, Steel, Water, and Poison to give it better defensive matchups, allowing it to set up in front of foes that would otherwise beat it one-on-one.

Draft Strategy

Raging Bolt's lack of support options as well as its struggle against bulkier specially defensive walls means that it often requires a lot of team support. As a round 1 pick, it often looks for teammates such as physical wallbreakers, entry hazard setters and removers, and Pokemon with higher Speed to help it out.

Physical Wallbreakers: Raging Bolt can struggle with breaking through specially defensive walls by itself, especially Ground-types. Pairing it with the likes of Landorus-T, Cinderace, and Weavile can help with this, as they can break through each other's checks, creating a powerful wallbreaking duo.

Entry Hazard Control: A lot of the time, Raging Bolt wants the opposing team to be weakened so that it can easily clean with Thunderclap. Hazards are one of the easiest ways to achieve this; some good hazard setters that pair well with it include Ting-Lu, Glimmora, and Gliscor. Raging Bolt also appreciates being able to run items other than Heavy-Duty Boots, so reliable spinners, such as Iron Treads, Terapagos, and Tentacruel, make for strong pairings.

Fast Teammates: Raging Bolt is plagued with a very mediocre Speed tier, meaning it often struggles against faster foes that do not get KOed by Thunderclap. It appreciates having partners with top-tier Speed such as Greninja, Meowscarada, and Darkrai, but it also appreciates base 95 through 110 Speed Pokemon such as Iron Crown, Urshifu-R, and Ogerpon-W to deny the opponent the ability to run damage-boosting natures on their Pokemon rather than Speed-boosting ones.

Healing Wish: Raging Bolt struggles with longevity, so it benefits heavily from teammates that can give it a second chance with Healing Wish. Alomomola is an extremely common pairing due to its ability to slowly pivot as well, but teammates like Mesprit and Jirachi also work well.

Dual Screens Support: Since Raging Bolt is reliant on being able to safely use Calm Mind a lot of the time, it appreciates additional opportunities generated from dual screens, whether that be from Prankster Klefki or teammates like Deoxys-S and Corviknight.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Grass- and Ground-types: While Draco Meteor can break through Grass- and Ground-types, Raging Bolt does not like being forced out afterwards, since it's a massive momentum sink to do so and provides the opponent a safe turn of setup. The likes of Iron Treads, Ting-Lu, and Rillaboom can be particularly annoying because they can survive a hit; they can then force it out or pivot to teammates that can capitalize on its lowered Special Attack after a Draco Meteor.

Physical Wallbreakers: Many common foes, especially ones that resist Thunderclap like Great Tusk, Meowscarada, and Garchomp, can reliably break through Raging Bolt with a Choice Band or super effective attacks, forcing it to pick specific Tera types to survive hits. Many foes can also chip Raging Bolt down enough so that it can be reliably KOed by a revenge killer afterwards.

Fast Encore / Substitute Users: Given the mass distribution of Encore, Raging Bolt can often find itself being locked into moves and forced out. Foes like Iron Valiant, Ogerpon-W, and Scream Tail can switch in on it and threaten it after it uses Calm Mind or force it into repeatedly using Thunderclap. Substitute, on the other hand, forces Raging Bolt to make difficult decisions if the foe would not survive a Thunderclap.

Chip Damage: Due to its lack of reliable recovery, Raging Bolt can easily get weakened by entry hazards, status effects, and weaker attacks, allowing strong wallbreakers to OHKO it more reliably later on in the match. This is especially threatening due to its low Speed, meaning most foes can easily pivot on it or chip it down if they resist or can play around Thunderclap.

movesets.name: Wallbreaker
movesets.description: Raging Bolt stands out as one of the premier special wallbreakers in the tier, boasting exceptional offensive stats and a formidable STAB combination. Lucarionite further amplifies its breaking power by granting it Adaptability and substantial stat boosts, whereas Diancite can be used to significantly raise its Speed stat, albeit at the cost of some firepower and bulk. Timid nature helps Diancite Raging Bolt outspeed Great Tusk, Arceus formes, and Eternatus; a Modest nature allows Lucarionite Raging Bolt to reach feats like OHKOing offensive Arceus-Ground after minimal entry hazard chip damage. Raging Bolt utilizes Draco Meteor for its immense firepower and hit-and-run potential with Volt Switch. Thunderbolt and Discharge provide options for either dealing more damage or fishing for paralysis, respectively. Additionally, Thunderclap allows Raging Bolt to reverse kill Pokemon such as Urshifu-R and Basculegion formes, and Volt Switch enables it go function as a strong pivot. Raging Bolt may also utilize moves such as Calm Mind and Substitute to serve as a devastating progress maker at the cost of Volt Switch's utility or Thunderclap's priority. It synergizes exceptionally well with pivots like Urshifu-R, Magearna, and Pecharunt to form incredible VoltTurn cores; Urshifu-R and the Latiasite versions of the latter two also deal with Ground-types such as Arceus-Ground and Great Tusk, with the former being able to check Blissey as well. Offensive partners such as Spectrier, Calm Mind Arceus formes, and Zamazenta also aid in dismantling opposing defensive cores and thus synergize well with Raging Bolt. Pairing Raging Bolt with hazard setters such as Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk and Magearna helps it secure KOs more efficiently, especially against foes such as Arceus formes. It faces troubles against Pixilate Extreme Speed users such as Dragonite and Regieleki; thus, it is usually paired with Pokemon such as Pecharunt and Arceus-Ground to deal with them.

movesets.name: Special Attack Booster Energy
movesets.description:
• Thunderbolt is Raging Bolt's most consistent STAB attack and beats Primarina, non-Assault Vest Metagross, and Volcanion.
  • Draco Meteor is Raging Bolt's strongest STAB attack and should be used against Skeledirge.
  • Thunderclap allows Raging Bolt to get KOs after using Thunderbolt and Draco Meteor and helps in matchups against some Hoopa-U sets as well as against Custap Berry users like Primarina and the Urshifu formes.
  • Taunt allows Raging Bolt to beat Pecharunt and Ogerpon-W.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Raging Bolt to survive the Choice Band Urshifu formes' Close Combat, while the Special Defense EVs allow it to survive a Hyper Beam from Timid Porygon-Z. The Speed EVs allow Raging Bolt to outspeed Modest Primarina. The remaining EVs are put in Special Attack to maximize power for best odds against specially defensive Primarina.
  • Draco Meteor into Thunderclap is stronger than Thunderbolt into Thunderclap, so in matchups where there is no recovery from the foe, such as against non-Sitrus Berry Annihilape, it is better to use Draco Meteor into Thunderclap.

movesets.name: Haban Berry
movesets.description:
• Thunderbolt is the main Electric-type STAB move, but Thunder makes Raging Bolt more reliable against Primarina, as Thunder can OHKO it, so you don't have to worry about potential Weakness Policy or Encore after using Calm Mind or Charge. Thunderbolt should be used when it does neutral or super effective damage against frailer foes like Primarina, Corviknight, and Metagross without an Assault Vest. Against foes that can survive Draco Meteor followed by Thunderclap like Hoopa-U and Urshifu-S, it is safer to use Thunderbolt or Thunder into Draco Meteor.
  • Draco Meteor hits Electric-resistant foes like Rillaboom and should be used against bulkier foes like Hoopa-U and Skeledirge. It also 2HKOes Unaware Skeledirge.
  • Thunderclap is a priority move that helps to KO low HP Pokemon like non-Assault Vest Metagross after one use of Thunderbolt. Draco Meteor into Thunderclap does slightly more damage than Thunderbolt into Thunderclap against neutral targets, but Thunder into Thunderclap does more. Thunderclap also counters Custap Berry users like Primarina and Hoopa-U by attacking on the turn they use their Custap Berry.
  • Calm Mind and Charge are both here to boost Raging Bolt's power and special bulk. Both moves especially help against Primarina, though Charge is more reliable against it and Calm Mind is useful in more matchups like against Rillaboom, Iron Hands, and Spectrier.
  • Haban Berry allows Raging Bolt to win against Dragon-types such as Walking Wake, as it can OHKO them after surviving a Dragon-type move. However, if those Dragon-types are holding a Haban Berry, Raging Bolt can't OHKO them and is 2HKOed back.

movesets.name: Calm Mind
movesets.description:
Raging Bolt's amazing bulk, high Special Attack stat, and great typing both defensively and offensively allow it to become a dangerous wallbreaker and sweeper, threatening common defensive pieces like Toxapex, Moltres, and Zapdos. Draco Meteor brings Raging Bolt exceptional power, allowing it to OHKO Ground-types like Landorus-T, Garchomp, a Great Tusk trying to switch into it, the former with a Calm Mind boost. However, Dragon Pulse is a great option if you want consistent damage, threatening the opposition for longer at a time. Weather Ball is an amazing option when paired with weather teams, as it removes Grass-types like Ferrothorn and Rillaboom in sun and threatens Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Iron Treads in rain. Dragonium Z gives Raging Bolt a one-time nuke, letting it obliterate most non-resistant foes, such as Gliscor and Galarian Slowking, with a Calm Mind boost, opening up its teammates. Do note that Dragonium Z should only be used with Draco Meteor, as the damage reduction with Dragon Pulse is quite noticeable. Booster Energy boosts Raging Bolt's Special Attack, allowing it to get OHKOs on Pokemon that it would normally run from, such as Iron Valiant with Thunderclap and Gliscor with Draco Meteor, both at +1. Leftovers lets it switch into Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Ogerpon-W more consistently, allowing it to set up easily.

Raging Bolt is best on more offensive teams that appreciate it wearing down other Pokemon like Toxapex, Moltres, and Ting-Lu. Its main weakness is Ground-types like Ting-Lu, Gliscor, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T, as they can come in on a Thunderbolt and threaten it out with a super effective Earthquake. Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Ogerpon-W, and Hisuian Samurott can help remove these foes for Raging Bolt, and in return, it can eliminate bulky Water-types like Toxapex, Alomomola, and Slowbro. Hisuian Samurott in particular, along with Ferrothorn and Heatran, can set up entry hazards for Raging Bolt in order to chip down Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Ting-Lu into KO range of its attacks quicker. Raging Bolt doesn't have the best Speed stat, and that can be taken advantage of by Pokemon like Weavile and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, which can bypass its Thunderclap either through their own priority for the former or Psychic Terrain for the latter and threaten to KO it. Steel-types like Melmetal, Kingambit, and Mega Scizor help in this regard, as well as absorbing Fairy-type attacks from Pokemon like Mega Diancie and Iron Valiant; Kingambit can also threaten Galarian Slowking and Mega Latios, two Pokemon that Raging Bolt has trouble with. In return, Raging Bolt can chip down Toxapex, Moltres, and Zamazenta for Kingambit’s own sweep later in the game. Finally, Raging Bolt fits very well on weather-based teams. On sun teams, Raging Bolt's Protosynthesis is activated, allowing it to hit harder; it also synergizes well with Mega Charizard Y, as Mega Charizard Y can switch into the Ground-type moves that Raging Bolt baits out while also dealing with Ferrothorn. In return, Raging Bolt can deal with Toxapex, Moltres, and Dragonite, which would otherwise give Mega Charizard Y trouble. Rain, on the other hand, gives Raging Bolt a Weather Ball capable of demolishing the Ground-types that would otherwise give it much trouble. In return, Raging Bolt provides a check for Grass- and Electric-types like Rillaboom, Zapdos, and Ogerpon-W that would give rain teams trouble.

movesets.name: Pivot
movesets.description:
Raging Bolt is an excellent pivot, using its stellar offensive presence and ability to force out Pokemon such as Toxapex, Zapdos, and Moltres to gain momentum for its teammates. Not only that, Raging Bolt's solid defensive typing makes it have favorable matchups against Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Mega Charizard Y. Thunderclap is a useful form of priority, being the main way Raging Bolt threatens out faster threats such as Urshifu-R, Iron Valiant, and Mega Medicham. Draco Meteor gives Raging Bolt the ability to hit Pokemon that would effortlessly block Volt Switch, such as Landorus-T and Gliscor. Taunt is an option over Thunderbolt, allowing Raging Bolt to stop entry hazards from being set up by the likes of Heatran and Ferrothorn and deny recovery for Pokemon like Mega Scizor, Blissey, and Garganacl. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Raging Bolt pivot safely in the face of hazards, particularly Spikes, while Dragonium Z gives Raging Bolt the ability to OHKO Gliscor and Landorus-T and muscle through weakened checks like Garganacl and Mega Tyranitar. Alternatively, Leftovers grants Raging Bolt more longevity to check Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Ogerpon-W, and Urshifu-R more consistently. When using Heavy-Duty Boots, an EV spread with maximum Special Attack and Speed is preferred. However, the second EV spread ensures Raging Bolt outspeeds defensive Landorus-T while also surviving a Landorus-T's Earthquake after Stealth Rock.

Raging Bolt fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, where its pivoting abilities are much appreciated to keep momentum and bring in wallbreakers such as Mega Medicham and Kingambit against Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking, and Mega Tyranitar. Raging Bolt checking Ogerpon-W and Tornadus-T is appreciated by teammates such as Alomomola and Great Tusk. In return, Alomomola provides Wish support, making up for Raging Bolt's poor longevity, and Great Tusk removes Spikes, which cut into Raging Bolt lacking Heavy-Duty Boots. Due to Raging Bolt's lack of power, it loves the Spikes set by teammates like Samurott-H and Ferrothorn, chipping down its checks such as opposing Ferrothorn and Heatran. Raging Bolt is also hindered by Ground-types that easily outpace it such as Garchomp and Great Tusk, since they also block its Volt Switch, stopping it from gaining momentum. Teammates that check these foes, such as Moltres and Landorus-T, are good partners for Raging Bolt.

movesets.name: Calm Mind (Electric)
movesets.description: Calm Mind Raging Bolt is a potent wallbreaker and setup sweeper for Electric teams, possessing a high Special Attack, excellent defenses, and incredible priority in Thunderclap to pick off faster foes like Sneasler and Ceruledge. With Devastating Drake, Raging Bolt breaks through bulkier targets like Mega Venusaur and Archaludon, and it also applies tremendous pressure on bulky Ground-types, having a high chance to KO Gliscor without a boost, OHKOing specially defensive Swampert at +1, and providing good odds to OHKO Water Absorb Clodsire at +1. With its typing, Raging Bolt switches in against foes like Mega Charizard Y and Ogerpon-W and threatens them out with its STAB moves. Thunderclap lets Raging Bolt revenge kill faster threats like Greninja and Enamorus as well as Iron Valiant at +1. 136 Speed EVs allow Raging Bolt to outspeed Jolly Ursaluna and specially defensive Heatran. Rotom-W and Zapdos provide crucial Ground-immune teammates for the team. Rotom-W can take on threats like Sand Rush Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Choice Scarf Landorus-T, and Zapdos can remove foes like Ferrothorn and Tapu Bulu and serve an offensive or defensive role, assisting against Ground and Fighting teams. Tapu Koko threatens Dragon- and Dark-types like Latios, Hydreigon, and Weavile, and with Grass Knot and Hidden Power Ice, it helps in alleviating Ground matchups, removing threats like Landorus. Tapu Koko also sets Electric Terrain to boost Raging Bolt's Electric-type moves, most notably allowing it to OHKO bulkier threats like Mega Diancie and Galarian Darmanitan with +1 Thunderclap. Iron Hands and Choice Band Zeraora eliminate special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Blissey as well as Ferrothorn while also covering Ice- and Dark-types like Kyurem and Mega Tyranitar. Regieleki and Alolan Raichu offer valuable speed control. Regieleki possesses incredible natural Speed, outspeeding Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Iron Valiant, and +1 Volcarona, while Alolan Raichu can outspeed +1 Roaring Moon, Choice Scarf Meowscarada, and even Sand Rush Excadrill when under Electric Terrain. Raging Bolt appreciates entry hazard control from teammates like Rotom-W, Zapdos, and Regieleki.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description: -The given EV spread allows Raging Bolt to survive Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao and outspeed Flutter Mane during Tailwind, allocating the remaining EVs into Special Attack.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description: • The alternative EV spread allows Raging Bolt to outspeed the vast majority of Tapu Fini in order to immediately threaten an OHKO. The remaining bulk is used to ensure Terastallized Raging Bolt is 3HKO'd by Jolly Chien Pao's Ice Spinner or Adamant Chien Pao's Sucker Punch.
